_meta.note: Adversarial DAG reviewer = a deterministic gate-quality auditor (both runtimes) + an agent-refutation layer (skill prompt). Applies refute-don't-confirm to the PLAN before it runs. Rules: hollow_gate (no behavioral criterion), ungated, unguarded_phase, existence/vacuous criteria, nondeterministic, gate_offphase. Node and Python auditors share one ruleset (parity seed → planning/parity-notes.md). Verified by both suites + dogfooded on our own DAGs.

tasks.title: Author fixtures + parity notes
tasks.description: Create shared DAG fixtures under planning/audit-fixtures/ (hollow.json with a `true` gate, existence.json with test -f, nondeterministic.json with curl, good.json fully behavioral) and planning/parity-notes.md capturing the shared classification regexes and the expected findings, so the node and python auditors can be checked for parity.

GATE_DA0.desc: Fixtures and parity notes exist and are meaningful.

GATE_DA1.desc: The node auditor catches weak gates and clears good ones.

review.prompt: Refute that DA1 is done: does the auditor ACTUALLY detect a hollow gate, or does it just parse? Is a phase with one behavioral + one test -f criterion correctly NOT flagged hollow? Is the auditor itself hollow (its own T42 assertions trivial)? Does a fully-behavioral DAG pass clean (no false positives)?

criteria.desc: suite covers the auditor (T42 group PASSED)

GATE_DA2.desc: The python auditor matches the node one.

criteria.desc: python auditor flags the hollow fixture
criteria.cmd: cd "$PROJECT_DIR/py" && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m heartbeat.cli audit "$PROJECT_DIR/planning/audit-fixtures/hollow.json" | grep -q hollow_gate

GATE_DA3.desc: Node and python agree; both suites green.

criteria.desc: node and python auditors agree on the good fixture (both exit 0)
criteria.cmd: node "$PROJECT_DIR/plugin/templates/hb-audit.js" "$PROJECT_DIR/planning/audit-fixtures/good.json" && cd "$PROJECT_DIR/py" && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m heartbeat.cli audit "$PROJECT_DIR/planning/audit-fixtures/good.json"
